accuracy.why: No fact, figure or claim of the sources is missing or added in the 161 strings (stage 4's fence: nothing removed, nothing restored), and the one loss on record is repaired: map.locate.err names the browser again. The palms figure is the source's figure in the Urdu scale (2.5 million = 25 lakh), not another number. Two points off for approximations: foot.independence and inline.home.title do not carry the brand the sources lead with (N1); cat.crafts.d commits to one reading of 'by local hands' («سب»); 'experiences' is now «سرگرمیاں» / «سرگرمی», narrower than the source word; list.empty says 'not found yet' where the source says 'none yet'; nav.blog («مضامین») and nav.dining («کھانے پینے کی جگہیں») name the content where the source names the format.

nativeness.why: For: the functional layer now reads as the reader's own interfaces do («مینو», «اشتراک کریں», «لنک کاپی ہو گیا ✓»), he called «مجھ سے کتنی دور؟» good natural Urdu and the 404 heading charming and clear, and the nine calibration labels drew no remark from a fourth reader. Six points off, counted cluster by cluster as the calibration counted them. The home page's marketing copy keeps the sources' images, which he heard as translated («زندگی کا وعدہ کرتا ہے», «ورثے کا دل», «نخلستان کو محسوس کرنے», «نمایاں ترین مقامات», «روح سمیٹ لیتے ہیں», «نچوڑ … آہنگ», «داستان» five times, home.route.s5.d with its split dates and «ترشاوہ پھلوں»); «سیاحتی رہنما» still reads first as a person in four strings; «راستہ» serves the trail pages, the two-day route and the breadcrumb; «حسی» is still letter for letter an Urdu adjective; «تقریبات», «قیام گاہیں» and «زمرہ» are stiff to him; list.lead still hangs its opening on an imperative. And nineteen strings carry this round's edits, the repair of his one serious remark among them, which no reader has seen.

compliance.why: Zero forbidden letterforms and zero non-Latin digits in the 161 strings after the edits; termbase names byte-identical («الاحساء» 16 times, «جبل القارہ», «قصر ابراہیم», «سوق القیصریہ», «العقیر», «مسجد جواثا»); every agreement was checked on a dictionary page at stage 5 and the edits touch three («لنک کاپی ہو گیا», «اپنی سیر», «فاصلے … دیے گئے ہیں»); every loan in the text has an entry that cites P16. Two points off: five entries are pending («حسی», «مفلق», «بندرگاہ», «حساوی لیموں کا باغ», «براؤزر»); three genders follow usage against a printed dictionary label («بندرگاہ», «ریت», «کھجوریں»); five loans enter in one round; and the two palm strings carry a converted figure that the stage checker reports until it is taught the conversion ruled under P10.

fit.why: The palms are counted in lakh, as this reader counts and as his paper writes this very figure («25 لاکھ سے زیادہ», «25 لاکھ+»); the location notice says where to look in his browser's own words («براؤزر میں اپنے مقام کی اجازت دیکھ لیں»); address is honorific throughout and no devotional frame was added; the header, the time pills and the figure card were measured on a build with these wordings. One point off: «قصر ابراہیم» above «قلعے» made him pause, «حسی» stops a reader, and the language button («UR») and the brand line stay in Latin on an Urdu page.

blind_reader_rulings.reason: «فہرست» → «مینو» and «مرکزی فہرست» → «مرکزی مینو» (changes a11y.menu and a11y.mainNav). Both are accessible names: on the page a visitor sees the three-bar button, a screen-reader user hears the word. Loan admitted under P16 on all three conditions: Android, Chrome and MediaWiki call the function «مینو» / «مینیو»; the reader stumbled; the word is a headword of both dictionaries.

Applied where the wording is the Urdu's own doing: det.nearby.d says «اپنی سیر مکمل کر سکتے ہیں», after the Arabic «جولتك». The rest is kept. «راستہ» is the common Urdu word for a route and for a path, as 'trail / route' and «مسار» are in the sources; the page behind «سیر کے راستے» lists routes that link sights, not day-by-day programmes, so his «سیر کا پروگرام» would promise something else, and «پروگرام» is a loan where a common Urdu word stands (P16). That the menu label reads as walking paths until the page opens is true of the English 'Trails' as well: logged with the source defects. The body of the calibration page is approved text and not in this batch.

«کھیت» → «فارم» in nav.leisure. Loan admitted under P16: a cultivated field is not what a farm one visits is called (press: «زرعی فارم»); the reader could not tell what the label offers; «فارَم» is a headword of Urdu Lughat. Within the measured header budget (need 1445px against 1478). «تفریح گاہیں اور باغات» (parks and gardens) is another group and stays; the lime farm keeps «باغ» in its name until the round that writes its page (entry pending): an orchard is a «باغ», and whether that name should follow the generic is for that round.

'Oasis Fruits' / «ثمار الواحة» does not say what the section holds in either source (the owner's navigation queue already lists this label as having no verb). «نخلستان کے پھل» says what the source says; a clearer label would be a different label, and it would have to be measured.

'Online Stores' / «المتاجر»: whose shops, and that the page is a directory of other people's shops, is not said in either source; that the footer carries no such link is the site's structure. The Urdu follows the English.

«میلے اور تقریبات» would add a word the source label does not carry ('Events', «الفعاليات») to three strings that share one English, and it is a bar label, where the bar has 33px to spare at its threshold and this label would about double (not measured: the wording falls on the first ground). «تقریبات» is the common word (Rekhta: «رسوم، اجتماعات، جشن»), and the card under it says «میلے» at once, as he found.

Understood, by his own account. «ہوٹل اور رہائش» adds hotels to a label that says 'Places to Stay' and brings a loan where a common Urdu word stands and is used of tourist lodging («سیاحوں کے لیے قیام گاہیں»): P16, and the reader's preference does not open the door. A bar label as well.

«تجربہ» → «سرگرمی» (his own word, from observation 18). The other half is the source's: it lists 'sights' and 'places' side by side («معلم … مكان»); stage 2 already set them apart as «سیاحتی مقام» and «جگہ».

The hint about Esc, the arrow keys and Enter is printed on phones in every language (Search.astro hides the shortcut badge below 620px, not this line): logged at stage 3. «تیر کے نشانوں» stays; no wording was offered and the keys carry no other Urdu name.

The sources have two tools and three names for planning: 'My saved places' / «معالمي المحفوظة» (the list), 'Plan your trip' / «خطّط لرحلتك» (the planning page), and a closing block that speaks of 'favourite sights' and 'arranging your days'. The Urdu keeps each as the source has it; the owner's navigation queue already carries 'three labels for planning'.

«اصل» goes from the skip link: «سیدھے مواد پر جائیں», as the English and Arabic say and as BBC Urdu and DW word the link. «مواد» stays in both strings: it is those sites' word for exactly this function. For a visitor on a phone both lines are an artifact of the plain-text page: the skip link is off screen until it takes keyboard focus, and «نیچے مواد پر جائیں» is the accessible name of an arrow.

«گائیڈ» is on the owner's list of banned loans (style_rules.anglicisms; role file 02 maps it to «رہنما»), and the stage checker reports it. The personal reading of «سیاحتی رہنما» is real (ur.wikipedia: a person in four pages of five) and is charged under nativeness; no other wording was offered.
'Begin the story' / «ابدأ الحكاية» is the label of a button that scrolls to the next section of the same page (href #name); neither source says so. «داستان شروع کریں» says what they say.

Open item P10, ruled in this round: counts in the Urdu scale, «25 لاکھ سے زیادہ» in the lead and «25 لاکھ+» on the figure card (changes home.hero.lead and inline.home.fact.palms.n). His expected form is the ruling.

The order he wrote: «لفظ “الاحساء”، “حسی” کی جمع ہے». Vowel signs on the Arabic word are not available (P8 guard on U+0650, ruling P17), and a language label would be an added fact. The homograph stays and is recorded in the entry «حسی».

No wording was offered, and the image is the source's in both languages ('a generous oasis promising life where no one expects it', «تَعِد بالحياة»). A coined image in its place would be wording nobody has read standing where faithful wording stood. Charged under nativeness.

It is the sources that call the six groupings 'paths' on the home page («اختر طريقك», «مساراتٌ تختصر لك الأحساء») and 'categories' on the list page («اختر فئةً»); the Urdu keeps the two words the Arabic keeps. 'Distil' and 'rhythm' are the source's too («نچوڑ», «آہنگ»).
«تجربات اور دستکاری» → «سرگرمیاں اور دستکاری», his wording. Whether the visitor does or watches is not said in either source ('by local hands', «بأيدي أهلها»): logged at stage 2.

«ہریس» is the sourced termbase form (the ur.wikipedia title, Wikidata Q16841203); «ہریسہ» is recorded in the entry as the Urdu cognate, for search. What the two dishes are is in no language of this card line, and a gloss cannot stand in one; the food pages say it when their round comes («مفلق» stays pending until then).
The home card lists mosques under historic landmarks ('Forts, palaces and mosques') and the index gives them a section of their own: the site's own structure, in every language.

«مشہور ترین» would change the claim: the Arabic says «أبرزُ معالم الواحة», the most prominent, not the most famous, and a superlative is bound by the Arabic (P19). No wording was offered for the second sentence, whose image is the source's ('capture the spirit of the place', «تختصر روح المكان»). Charged under nativeness.
No wording was offered, and both images are the sources' ('The heritage heart', «قلب التراث»; 'to feel the oasis', «لتلمس روح الواحة»). Charged under nativeness.
The pill now says «دن میں». His «دوپہر» would put noon where both sources say daytime: a fact the source does not carry.

The three labels are three different times in the source ('Evening', 'Late afternoon', 'Sunset'; «المساء», «آخر العصر», «الغروب»); one word for two of them would erase a distinction the Arabic makes. «غروب آفتاب» is the plain Urdu for sunset, and «ڈھلتی سہ پہر» is the only candidate that keeps 'late'.

Open item P3c, ruled as far as labels go: a name stands bare in a label, a list or a title and the plain Urdu generic stands near it, never next to it. His pause is the cost of a name whose Arabic generic says 'palace' over a line that says 'fort' — which is exactly what the Arabic source has («قصر إبراهيم», «الحصن»). The gloss form for running text stays open (batch b1).

Which story, and why the mosque is worth the morning, is not said in either source ('one of the oldest stories in Islam', «واحدةً من أقدم حكايات الإسلام»). «داستان» is the batch's word for 'story' («حكاية») and Rekhta gives it as the detailed account of the events of a person or a people, 'history'.

(a) The site rule keeps «الحساوي» inside this proper name and nowhere explains it; (b) the English name is as descriptive ('Hasawi Lime Farm'), and on the page it is a link in the place of a name; (d) the line is a verbless fragment in both sources and neither says whether visitors pick. (c) «ترشاوہ پھل» is the standard Urdu for citrus and no wording was offered. The Urdu's own share — the dates set between two commas inside the phrase — is recorded for the next round, with the reorder that puts them last as the sources do; not changed in a round that gets no blind read of it.
